title: Time between failures of a booster pump

AtMost.says: You used λ = 400. 400 hours is the mean; the rate is λ = 1/400 per hour.
That is P(X > 200), the chance the pump lasts past 200 hours. "Fails within 200 hours" is P(X ≤ 200) = 1 − e^(−λx).

MoreThan.says: You used x = 500, the pump's whole age. The exponential is memoryless: the 300 hours already run do not count, only the 200 more.
That is the chance it fails within the next 200 hours. The question asks the chance it keeps running: P(X > 200).

Quantile.says: That is the 90th percentile, the time by which 90 % have failed. Solve 1 − e^(−λx) = 0.10.
You used λ = 400. 400 hours is the mean; the rate is λ = 1/400 per hour.

hints: The rate is one over the mean: λ = 1/400 = 0.0025 per hour.
P(X ≤ x) = 1 − e^(−λx). For the pump that has run 300 hours, the memoryless property says P(X > 300 + 200 | X > 300) = P(X > 200).
